answer.rationale: Run a small, guarded referral-incentive test among established customers. Prior evidence shows qualified revenue gains without measurable retention harm, making this more consistent with sustainable growth than broad discounting. The recovered discount experiment produced a 12% decline in 30-day retention despite strong acquisition, so promotional pricing should not be generalized as the response to the competitor’s price cut. Referral incentives will not directly resolve all price-sensitive SMB churn, so monitor retention and qualified revenue closely.
